name: Ly Cong Uan
role: Founder of the Lý dynasty who moved the capital from Hoa Lư to Đại La in 1010 and renamed it Thăng Long.
known_facts: Born in 974 in Cổ Pháp, raised in a Buddhist pagoda.
Served as a military officer under the Early Lê dynasty.
Was acclaimed emperor in 1009 after the death of Lê Long Đĩnh.
Issued the Edict on Moving the Capital (Chiếu dời đô) in 1010.
Moved the court from Hoa Lư to Đại La and renamed the site Thăng Long, 'ascending dragon'.
Reigned under the name Thuận Thiên as the first emperor of the Lý dynasty.
interpretation: A man in his mid-thirties, tall and lean but broad-shouldered, with an oval face, high forehead, calm steady eyes, a thin moustache and a short sparse beard. Black hair gathered in a topknot under a black lacquered gauze cap. He wears a yellow silk robe with wide sleeves and faint woven dragon roundels, a dark red sash, and soft black leather boots. Signature accessory: a white paper folding fan with plain wooden ribs, held in his right hand.
